title: Find a missing side using area and a quadratic model

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: A right-angled triangle has base (x + 3) cm and height (x - 1) cm. Its area is 16 cm^2. Form an equation and find x.
student_prompt: Use area = 1/2 x base x height.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: For a triangle, area is half base times height, so include the factor 1/2.
x = -7 makes the side lengths negative, so use x = 5.

hint_ladder.title: Which area formula applies?
hint_ladder.prompt: This is a triangle, so the area formula includes a half. Start with the geometry before doing algebra.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Put the base and height expressions into the triangle area formula, then clear the fraction before expanding.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students use the rectangle area formula by accident, or forget to reject a value that makes a side length impossible.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For geometry modelling, choose the correct formula, substitute algebraic side expressions, solve the resulting quadratic, and check the context. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is applying the triangle area formula.

common_errors: does not multiply both sides by 2
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is clearing the half and rearranging.
The stuck point is solving and checking x in the geometry context.

mark_scheme_notes: Award marks for triangle area equation, clearing the half, rearranging, factorising, and contextual value.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: forgetting the 1/2 factor and failing to reject a negative side length.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, which area formula applies to this shape?
